scope: Paper identity, claim/population scope and study-design provenance only; no human scientific approval.
partial_paper: Stahl2011 was still running at capture. Its single completed candidate was captured but held; the paper is absent from the 168-paper checkpoint.
identity_check: Every new claim and population inspected against its named source PDF. No adjacent-article contamination found. Two study-design categorization issues held; original source records preserved.

quarantined.reason: PDF p. 1 identifies a longitudinal observational study; p. 4 describes a comparison of eight word-retrieval-treatment participants with usual care to check a potential confound. The draft labels method=clinical_RCT, although no randomized trial is established by this source. Reconcile observational comparison versus randomized-trial provenance before publication.

PDF pp. 1, 3–6 and 8 describe experimental singing/rhythmic-speech task conditions and immediate articulatory performance in 17 participants, rather than longitudinal therapy efficacy. The draft is categorized as a therapy with relationship=treatment_response. Reconcile immediate task facilitation versus treatment outcome before publication.

source_papers.identity_scope: Primary cohort of first symptomatic stroke at 1–2 weeks: 132 recruited, 100 retained after imaging exclusions. Nine added claims match the current FC/lesion prediction, interhemispheric and intrahemispheric results, and multitask analysis on PDF pp. 1–6. The overall cohort n=100 is distinguished in the source from domain-specific available-case counts.

Longitudinal observational connectometry study, n=22 early subacute (2–6 weeks), n=15 chronic follow-up (>6 months). Five retained claims match QA-comprehension/production and corpus-callosum lesion-load results on PDF pp. 4–5. The clinical_RCT-labeled treatment comparison R007 is held.

Neural Plasticity article 8740353, Right Hemisphere Remapping of Naming Functions Depends on Lesion Size and Location in Poststroke Aphasia. Primary chronic cohort: 49 recruited, 39 retained. Twelve claims match lesion-size, ROI remapping and naming analyses, especially PDF pp. 3–5 and 9. Distinguished from the separate Human Brain Mapping article by the same authors.

Human Brain Mapping 38:2051–2066, DOI 10.1002/hbm.23504. Primary chronic cohort: 46 recruited, 32 retained; n=24 successful/unsuccessful naming subset. Fourteen claims match PCAD, hierarchical regressions, activity and lesion-site results on PDF pp. 6–11. Not treated as an independent replication of the same-authors Neural Plasticity cohort.

Primary CSD tractography study of 17 subacute left-ischaemic-stroke participants with aphasia and 10 controls, native Arabic speakers, mean MRI timing 3.07 weeks. Three claims match current diffusion/HSS associations and the FAT null on PDF pp. 3 and 6.

Experimental melody/rhythm/lyrics study of 17 nonfluent aphasic participants. The sole captured record is held because its treatment-response categorization does not distinguish immediate task performance from therapy efficacy.
